That's being said, all these icons have their labels in on-screen text too, so making the icons bigger is not crucial for both readability and ease of activation (excl. the "X" close buttons which do not have an on-screen text for them, thus may be missed by users with magnification)

I think this over-states the benefits
Not as big of a fan of this version bc it's a bit vague. I love the specificity of the other 3 options that call out the benefits: it's new, no clutter, faster, etc.

Riff on these two, and making it less about YOUR faves since those vary: 

Fresh menu, faster flow 
Quic access to fave features like bookmarks, history, settings.
I don't mind the body of this one, but saying "Speed" in the headline makes me think of performance. Maybe to an average user it doesn't read like that. A riff could be "Tap in to a faster menu"
I like this header. For body, maybe you could tighten to: Quick access to your favorite features.

Haven't we heard in research that people perceive Fx to have an outdated look/be really slow? 

I like this version bc it addresses those things :)

I like that the headline mentions 'menu' so it is clear what you're talking about. Alt subcopy to consider: 

Bookmarks, history, settings... all at your fingertips.

Are we thinking this would point to our mobile Release Notes? If so, I'm not really sure that the resulting content is worth the real estate here today. There's probably a lot more we could be doing with the release notes page.

@Emily Wachowiak I wonder if we could have one with a FX value prop header and a subtext that talks more about the process to set Firefox as default and makes it sound easy, quick, reversible, non-committal
Do we have a value prop for mobile-only users? Like sync to backup or something?
Maybe a shorter riff: Get lightning-fast browsing with privacy by default.
I'm assuming we don't have guidelines, capitalizing this made me glance twice but I think it makes sense like this.
Tough riff! I was trying to find a different way to say, "other data"

Riff:

Sign in to get passwords, bookmarks, and more
Leading with sync is helpful here
Just to throw a backup riff in here H: Sign in to sync B: Back up your passwords and more
Leading with value prop, and idea of 'saving' which might be more accessible than syncing?
Alt body: Sync passwords, bookmarks, history...  (use ellipses to hint at more)
H: Sign in to sync B: Instantly access passwords and more
The "get passwords" riffs don't work as well for me because they don't convey syncing - ie, taking your stuff with you
If we get to experiment, maybe a variant with "Sign up" could prompt people, since most people don't have an account

I like this string but tragic that it's 2 lines :( 

Riff: 
Privacy, speed, and fully customizable for you.
in contrast to something that sounds transactional, what if you double down on fox
It's giving Portlandia

Subcopy riff: 
* Make super fast browsing your default

Would we consider a version that is transcactional - reads like it is a system prompt and less like an ad. 

[Image connoting function] Make Firefox your default browser 
[No body]

when we did a set to default experiment ages ago "open all my links with firefox" was the winner iirc

the clarity of what "set to default" means is sometimes wonky. but i think "default" ubiquitous enough tbh
i like this headline. since they're already using fx, using the second line to preempt objections or obstacles it good
This one jumps out as a disconnect since the user has, in theory, switched by installing and using it
I think there was a riff that was similar in mobile onboarding and this one resonated! Leading with speed and privacy seem like they could be effective!
I like this one because it's less "browser speak"
